title: Improve Plan tab readability & polish
description:
## Goal
Make the Plan tab easier to read with a nicer look & feel.

## Scope / Requirements
- Break up the plan into sections: **This Week**, **Next Week**, **Later**.
- Remove the large **Best Next** section; instead **highlight the best next action inline** using visual treatment (e.g., badge, accent color, card emphasis) to draw attention without dominating the page.
- Due date is currently a timestamp; reduce to **day of week + date** (e.g., "Tue, Feb 5").

## Definition of Done
- Plan tab information hierarchy is clearer (sections + scannable typography/spacing).
- Best next action is visually emphasized but there is **no** oversized dedicated "Best Next" block.
- Due dates show weekday + date (no time), consistently across the Plan tab.
notes: Design reference: designs/be-7hw/design.md (includes screenshot alternative2_plan_tab.png + prototype code).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Edge cases covered (items due today, end-of-week boundary, missing dueDate).

title: Use raw Classroom assignments as chat candidates (no task splitting)
description:
## Context
Chat candidates are currently plan items (already split into smaller steps). This epic changes the *LLM candidate input* to be raw Classroom assignments, so the coach chooses from real assignments rather than pre-split plan tasks.

## Scope
Includes:
- Define the candidate schema for *raw Classroom assignments* (fields + truncation rules)
- Decide and document the selection/response contract (what ID is selected and what the API returns)
- Update `/chat/send` to build candidates from raw assignments
- Update coach prompts to match the contract (overview vs selection vs continuation)
- Update/extend automated tests to enforce the contract

Excludes (explicit non-goals):
- End-to-end redesign of weekly planning/planner (separate epic)
- Changing Google Classroom import behavior (separate epic)
- Large iOS UX redesign beyond what the API contract requires

## Key Decisions (must be explicit)
1) **Selection ID + API response shape** (choose ONE approach)
- **Option A (minimal iOS churn)**: keep `CoachDecision.selected_plan_item_id` selecting a *PlanItem id*, but make candidates raw assignments only for context. (Coach recommends an assignment in text, but selection stays plan-item.)
- **Option B (assignment-native)**: introduce `selected_assignment_id` (and likely a response field like `best_next_assignment`) so the app can highlight the chosen assignment.
- **Option C (hybrid)**: coach selects assignment id, and backend maps it to a best-next PlanItem (if possible) and returns both.

2) **Threading / continuation (“ok/ja”)**
- Define what entity is persisted as the “last selected” thread key (plan item vs assignment) and ensure the ack logic continues the same thread.

3) **Post-selection behavior**
After an assignment is selected, do we:
- ask one clarifying question, OR
- give a 30–120s first step, OR
- run just-in-time task-splitting for that one assignment?

## Deliverables
- A written contract doc (schema + rules + examples)
- Debug traces showing `/chat/send` candidates are raw assignments (and selected IDs validate against candidates)
- Prompt updates aligned to the contract

## Success Criteria
- `/chat/send` candidates are raw Classroom assignments (no breakdown) and include sufficient fields for grounding
- The coach reliably selects a relevant assignment when the user expresses a preference (measured via evals)
- No increase in invented details (measured via evals + spot-checking traces)

## Risks / Notes
- The current backend/iOS schemas are plan-item centric (`selected_plan_item_id`, `best_next_action: PlanItem`). If we choose Option B/C, we must update:
  - `backend/app/models/agent.py`
  - `backend/app/models/schemas.py`
  - iOS models + API client
- Long descriptions/attachments can bloat prompts; schema must include truncation rules.

title: Define raw-assignment candidate schema + selection contract (source of truth)
description:
## Why this task exists (epic alignment)
This is the “contract/spec” ticket. It removes ambiguity so implementation and prompt work don’t drift.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Decide which contract option we are implementing (A/B/C from epic) and record the decision.
- Candidate schema for raw assignments is specified (fields + meaning + truncation):
  - Required: `id`, `title`, `courseName`, `dueDate`, `description`, `url`
  - Notes on attachments: whether they live inside `description` (current behavior) or as a separate field
  - Truncation limits for `description`
- Threading/continuation rules are specified:
  - What is stored as “last selected” (plan item id vs assignment id)
  - How the ack set (“ok/ja/yes”) continues the thread
- Overview vs selection behavior is specified:
  - Overview question (“what else / what do I have / what subjects”) must keep selection null
  - Explicit preference (“English today”) must select a matching candidate when possible
- Provide at least 6 concrete examples (input → expected decision fields), including:
  - Greeting
  - Overview question
  - Explicit subject preference
  - Ambiguous preference
  - Ack continuation
  - Missing details (no description / no due date)

## Non-goals
- Implement backend changes (be-crg.2)
- Tune prompts beyond expressing the contract (be-crg.3)

## Output / Artifact
- A short markdown doc in the repo (preferred) or in ticket notes that other tickets reference by link/path.
notes:
Contract decision recorded in `docs/RAW_ASSIGNMENT_CANDIDATES_CONTRACT.md`

Decision: Option C (hybrid)
- candidates = raw Classroom assignments
- model selects `selected_assignment_id`
- backend maps to `best_next_action: PlanItem` via sourceAssignmentId for iOS compatibility

Key additions required in backend: `selected_assignment_id`, `mark_done_assignment_id`, and persistence of `last_selected_assignment_id`.

title: Backend: build chat candidates from Classroom assignments
description:
## Why this task exists (epic alignment)
Implements the epic’s core behavior change: build LLM candidates from raw Classroom assignments (no plan-item breakdown).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `/chat/send` constructs candidates from raw assignments returned by `select_assignments(user_id)`.
- Candidate payload matches the schema defined in `be-crg.1` (including truncation rules).
- Selection validation matches the chosen contract option:
  - If selecting assignment IDs, validate against assignment candidate IDs.
  - If selecting plan item IDs, ensure the logic remains correct and does not pretend candidates are plan items.
- Threading/continuation behavior (“ok/ja”) remains coherent per the contract decision.
- Debug export traces demonstrate:
  - `candidates` are raw assignments
  - raw model output is captured (when debug export enabled)
  - selected ID (if any) is one of the candidate IDs
- Tests updated/added to enforce the contract (at minimum):
  - candidate construction uses assignments
  - selection ID validation
  - ack continuation doesn’t switch subjects

## Files / Interfaces likely impacted (make changes as needed)
- `backend/app/routes/chat.py` (candidate construction + validation + threading)
- `backend/app/models/agent.py` (decision schema) **if** Option B/C
- `backend/app/models/schemas.py` (API response/request types) **if** Option B/C
- iOS models/API client **if** response shape changes

## Non-goals
- Weekly plan generation changes
- Classroom import behavior changes

## Notes
Keep the contract decision written and referenced; avoid partial implementations (e.g., assignment candidates but plan-item validation).

title: Update coach prompts for raw-assignment candidates
description:
## Why this task exists (epic alignment)
Align prompts with the raw-assignment candidate contract so the model selects correctly and avoids hallucinating details.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `coach_system.txt` + `coach_user.txt` are updated to match the contract decision from `be-crg.1`:
  - candidates are the source of truth
  - overview vs selection vs continuation rules are explicit
  - selection ID field name and allowed values are explicit
- Prompt guidance drives correct behaviors:
  - Overview question → overview answer AND selection field is null
  - Explicit preference → selects matching candidate when possible
  - Ack continuation → continues same thread, does not switch
- Add/adjust tests to reduce regressions:
  - prompt formatting smoke test
  - at least one behavior test asserting overview keeps selection null

## Non-goals
- Rewriting the entire coach personality
- Backend candidate construction changes (be-crg.2)

## Notes
Avoid conflicting instructions between system and user prompts. Keep curly-brace/JSON guidance consistent.

title: Deployment infrastructure for Study Buddy backend
description:
## Context
We need a repeatable way to deploy the backend with proper config/secrets and basic observability for an **iOS-only pilot (10–20 users)**.

## Decision
- Hosting target: **Render**
- Environments: **single demo environment** (add staging later if needed)

## Scope
Includes:
- Render Web Service setup using `backend/Dockerfile`
- Secrets and env var configuration in Render (no `.env` committed)
- DB/persistence plan for the pilot (SQLite volume vs managed Postgres)
- Basic observability (request id, logs) and a runnable smoke test
- iOS configuration steps (Base URL) + validation checklist

Excludes (explicit non-goals):
- Multi-region / autoscaling / high availability
- Full production SRE posture

## Success Criteria
- Backend is reachable over HTTPS at a stable URL
- `/health` returns OK and includes `X-Request-ID` response header
- Auth flows used in the pilot work (at minimum: session token + required endpoints)
- Pilot smoke test runbook exists and can be executed by a non-developer
- No secrets are committed to git; all secrets managed via Render

## Notes
We already have packaging + basic request id middleware; remaining work is Render configuration + runbook + iOS baseURL.

title: Render: configure env vars + secrets
description:
## Acceptance Criteria
### Render configuration (must be reproducible)
- Render service has the following env vars set (no secrets in git):
  - `SESSION_SECRET` (required)
  - `OPENAI_API_KEY` (required for /chat/send and /plan/week)
  - `OPENAI_MODEL` (optional)
  - `OPENAI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (optional)
  - `SQLITE_PATH` (required for persistence choice; see `be-jwg.6`)
  - `DEBUG_EXPORT_ENABLED` = `false` (recommended for pilot)

### Google OAuth (if Classroom is required for the pilot)
- Render service has these env vars set:
  - `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`
  - `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` (required for “Web application” clients)
  - `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI` = `https://<render-service-domain>/auth/google/callback`
- Google Cloud Console OAuth client has Authorized redirect URI updated to match the Render callback URL exactly.

### Validation
- Service boots and core endpoints work (no 5xx):
  - `GET /health`
  - `GET /plan/week` (authenticated)
  - `POST /chat/send` (authenticated)
- Classroom validation (if enabled): `GET /classroom/assignments` works after auth.

## Notes
- Dependencies:
  - Requires `be-jwg.4` (we need the Render domain to set `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI`)
  - Requires `be-jwg.6` (we need a decision on SQLite disk vs Postgres to set `SQLITE_PATH`)
- Reference: `docs/OAUTH_SETUP.md` redirect URI section.

title: iOS pilot: set Base URL + smoke test checklist
description:
## Acceptance Criteria
- iOS app points to Render backend URL (Debug Settings Base URL)
- Smoke test checklist exists and is runnable:
  - `/health`
  - sign-in (if required)
  - `GET /plan/week`
  - `POST /chat/send`
  - verify debug export behavior expectations (if enabled in pilot)
- Define what “success” looks like for a pilot session (latency + failure handling)
notes:
Observed in pilot: /chat/send intermittently returns 400 (Bad Request). iOS currently maps any non-401/503 to "Could not reach backend", which is misleading.

Backend returns 400 when payload is missing current_plan or current_plan.items (see backend/app/routes/chat.py).
Hypothesis: iOS sometimes calls sendChat with currentPlan=nil (plan not loaded) or empty items.

Next steps for this ticket:
- Add client-side guard: if weeklyPlan is nil/empty, force reload plan and block chat send with clear UI message
- Improve error handling: treat 400 as "Plan missing/out of sync; reload plan" instead of "Could not reach backend"
- Add a smoke test step: open Plan tab and ensure plan loaded before sending chat; verify no 400s

Implementing fix: prevent /chat/send calls unless current_plan is present and non-empty. If plan fetch fails, do NOT call chat; show a clear error instead. No fallback best_next_action.
Implemented real fix for 400 /chat/send (missing current_plan):
- iOS now blocks /chat/send unless weeklyPlan exists and has items
- If plan fetch fails, shows clear message instead of calling chat
- APIClient surfaces 400 as badRequest to improve diagnosis

Next: build/run iOS and verify no 400s during chat; then close be-jwg.7.
More hardening shipped (commit 264939a):
- iOS ChatView now preloads weekly plan on open (reduces chance of missing current_plan)
- iOS shows clearer error for badStatus(code) instead of generic "Could not reach backend"
- Backend /chat/send logs exact 400 reason: user_message_required vs current_plan_missing vs current_plan_items_empty (and returns more specific 400 detail for empty items)

Next: After deploying/building iOS, if 400 still happens, Render logs will now show which reason.
Confirmed by user: issue resolved. Closing be-jwg.7.

title: Assignment → Task breakdown & task presentation revamp
description:
## Context
We want to update how raw Classroom assignments (and attached Google Doc/Drive links) are turned into user-facing tasks, and how those tasks are presented in the app.

Current state (for reference):
- Chat candidates are **raw assignments** (no splitting).
- Weekly plan items are generated by the LLM planner (`plan_system.txt`) and validated via rails.

## Goals
- Improve/adjust the Assignment → Task breakdown logic (what constitutes a task, chunking rules).
- Improve task presentation: what information is shown (title, due date, course, links, instructions excerpts, etc.).
- Keep a clear contract between backend plan output and iOS UI.

## Non-goals (for this epic)
- OAuth / Classroom syncing changes beyond what’s needed for task content.
- Parsing full Google Doc contents (unless explicitly added as a sub-ticket).

## Work breakdown (sub-tickets to be added)
- Define updated task schema/contract and examples.
- Update planner prompt + rails to enforce the new contract.
- Update backend mapping logic (assignment ↔ plan items ↔ selection).
- Update iOS presentation and any UI affordances.
- Add/adjust tests and debug exports as needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Agreed contract for what fields are used to break assignments into tasks
- Weekly plan generation produces actionable, user-friendly task titles and metadata
- iOS task presentation updated per sub-tickets
- Backward compatibility decisions documented (or removed intentionally)

title: Remove task chunking heuristics (no page-range subranges / no assignment splitting)
description:
## Context
We want to remove “extra logic” that breaks an assignment into smaller task chunks.

Examples to remove (and similar breakdown guidance):
- "use assignment description (including any Attachments block) to break work into meaningful chunks"
- "if description includes page ranges (e.g. pages 34-64), start with an early subrange (e.g. pages 34-42)"

## Scope
- Update `backend/app/prompts/plan_system.txt` (and any other prompt/docs) to remove chunking instructions.
- Identify and remove any similar chunking logic in backend planning code (if present).

## Notes
- Keep the weekly plan schema + rails valid; we may need to adjust expectations around `estimatedMinutes` and titles once chunking is removed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Weekly plan prompt no longer instructs the model to break a single assignment into multiple smaller chunks (e.g., page-range subranges)
- Planning output remains valid under rails (10–20 min, <=15 items, actionable titles)
- Tests updated/added to confirm no chunking behavior is required
- Documented decision: tasks represent whole assignments (or one task per assignment) unless explicitly reintroduced

title: Add attachment links per task (plan item)
description:
## Context
Right now, Classroom attachments are folded into `Assignment.description` (an `Attachments:` text block) and the planner can use that text, but plan items themselves don’t carry structured attachment links.

## Goal
For each task/plan item shown in the app, expose **tappable attachment links** (title + URL) that come from the source assignment’s Classroom materials.

## Proposed approach (to be confirmed in implementation)
- Add a structured field to the plan item contract, e.g. `attachments: [{"title": string, "url": string}]` (or similar).
- Populate it by carrying forward assignment materials from `classroom.py` normalization.
- Update iOS UI to render links per item.

## Scope
- Backend: schema + planning output + mapping logic.
- iOS: display links for each item.
- Tests/docs: update contract docs and add coverage.

## Out of scope
- Parsing Google Doc body contents.
acceptance_criteria:
- Plan item contract includes a structured attachments/links field (title + url)
- For tasks sourced from Classroom assignments, attachment links are populated correctly
- iOS displays the links per task and tapping opens the URL
- Backward compatibility handled (field optional) and documented
- Tests updated/added for schema validation + end-to-end response shape

title: Adjust estimatedMinutes constraints for non-chunked tasks
description:
## Context
Today the weekly plan contract enforces `estimatedMinutes` between 10–20 minutes (prompt + rails). If we stop breaking assignments into smaller chunks, that constraint may no longer be realistic.

## Goal
Adjust the `estimatedMinutes` constraint so it matches the new “no chunking/splitting” approach.

## Scope
- Update planner prompt constraints in `backend/app/prompts/plan_system.txt`.
- Update backend validation/rails in `backend/app/services/rails.py` (and any related limits/constants).
- Update tests that assert the 10–20 minute range.
- Ensure iOS can display the updated range (and any UI copy that assumes 10–20).

## Notes / options to decide
- Option A: allow wider range (e.g. 10–120) but keep caps.
- Option B: make `estimatedMinutes` optional/null for whole-assignment tasks.
- Option C: introduce a separate field (e.g. `starterMinutes` vs `totalMinutes`).
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision recorded on the new `estimatedMinutes` policy (range/optional/new fields)
- `plan_system.txt` updated to match the policy
- `rails.py` enforces the new policy (and rejects/normalizes invalid values)
- Tests updated accordingly
- iOS renders the new values correctly (no hardcoded 10–20 assumptions)

title: Student-agent simulation harness for prompt optimization (P0)
description:
## Goal
Build a test environment that can:
1) run simulated student ↔ Study Buddy conversations
2) store full traces (inputs/outputs/tools/validation)
3) score runs with deterministic checks + LLM judges
4) compare prompt versions (A/B) and prevent regressions
5) support iteration loops for prompt optimization

## Definition of done
- One command (local + CI) can run the “quick suite” and produce:
  - trace artifacts
  - eval scores
  - A/B comparison report
- A “golden set” of scenarios is versioned and reproducible.
- Study Buddy agent prompt versions are tracked and comparable.

## Conventions (Beads)
- Ticket types:
  - Epic → multi-week deliverable
  - Task → shippable unit (1–3 days)
- Priority:
  - P0: blocks core loop
  - P1: improves correctness/velocity
  - P2: nice-to-have
- Dependencies:
  - Use Beads dependencies so `bd ready` shows unblocked work.

## Milestones
### Milestone A — Core loop (first usable)
- sim-harness.1 → sim-harness.2 → sim-harness.3 → sim-harness.4 → sim-harness.5 → sim-harness.6

### Milestone B — Measurable quality + regression prevention
- sim-harness.7 → sim-harness.8

### Milestone C — Team-ready + scalable iteration
- sim-harness.9 → sim-harness.11 → sim-harness.10

title: sim-harness.1 — Repo + project skeleton + developer workflow (P0)
description:
## Problem
Without a clean skeleton, everything becomes ad-hoc scripts and you lose reproducibility.

## Deliverables
- `sim/` package (Python recommended)
- `scenarios/` fixtures directory
- `prompts/` versioned prompts directory
- `results/` ignored outputs directory
- `Makefile` or `justfile` with standard commands:
  - `make quick`, `make full`, `make ab`, `make report`

## Acceptance criteria
- New dev can run `make quick` and get at least one simulated conversation + stored trace JSON.

## Design choices
- Python for eval ecosystem + JSON schema tooling.
- Keep harness separate repo or as `/tools/sim/` in monorepo.

title: sim-harness.10 — Privacy + safety + policy constraints (P1)
description:
## Problem
Even synthetic data can drift into real PII patterns; also the student may request cheating/answers.

## Deliverables
- Synthetic scenario guidelines (no real names/emails)
- Redaction hooks for later real logs (hash identifiers)
- Safety checks:
  - detect “give me the answer” requests
  - ensure Study Buddy responds with allowed assistance style
- Documented data retention policy for traces

## Acceptance criteria
- Suite never writes raw PII by default.
- Known “cheating prompt” scenarios are handled correctly.

## Depends on
- sim-harness.2
- sim-harness.7

title: sim-harness.11 — Prompt experimentation workflow + baselines (P1)
description:
## Problem
Prompt iteration becomes chaotic unless you standardize baselines and promotion rules.

## Deliverables
- Prompt registry:
  - `prompts/v001/`, `v002/`…
  - metadata: purpose, changes, expected impact
- Baseline locking:
  - “current best” pointer file
- A/B runner:
  - `make ab BASE=v010 CAND=v011`

## Acceptance criteria
- You can bisect regressions (“when did this scenario start failing?”).
- “Promote prompt” is a deliberate step with documented rationale.

## Depends on
- sim-harness.9

title: sim-harness: Reproducibility & determinism (run config + seed + prompt version pinning)
description:
## Goal
Make simulation runs reproducible so prompt changes can be compared reliably.

## Context
This belongs to the student↔coach simulation harness (`be-sim`). Reproducibility is critical for prompt optimization: without consistent run configuration (seed/model/prompt version), it’s hard to tell whether a change improved the prompt or just changed randomness.

Likely code areas (to be created/updated by this ticket’s implementation):
- Simulation runner/orchestrator module (e.g., `sim_harness/runner.py`, `sim_harness/orchestrator.py`)
- Prompt/version registry (e.g., `sim_harness/prompts/` or config)
- Trace writer (e.g., `sim_harness/trace.py`)

## Acceptance checks
- A `run_config` exists (file or CLI flags) capturing: prompt version id, model, temperature/top_p (if used), random seed, max turns, scenario selection.
- Orchestrator, Student simulator, and SUT wrapper all accept an explicit seed and use it consistently.
- Each trace artifact includes full `run_config` + prompt version identifiers in metadata.
- Running the same scenario twice with the same `run_config` produces identical outputs when using deterministic stubs, and “expected variability” is documented when using real LLM calls.

## Constraints
- Prefer a single source of truth for run configuration (avoid duplicated flags/config parsing across modules).
- If real LLM calls are used, document nondeterminism explicitly and keep evaluation comparisons robust to minor variations.

## Links
- Parent epic: `be-sim`
- Related: `be-sim.5` (orchestrator), `be-sim.6` (trace store), `be-sim.11` (prompt experimentation workflow)

title: sim-harness: Configurable retry limit (default 1 per conversation test)
description:
## Goal
Limit cost/time from retries during conversation tests and make retry behavior explicit + configurable.

## Context
This belongs to the simulation harness (`be-sim`). Without a retry cap, transient errors (timeouts, 5xx, rate limits) can cause runaway cost and long CI/local runs. You requested a quick fix: configurable retry limit with default 1 per conversation test.

Likely code areas (to be created/updated by this ticket’s implementation):
- Runner/orchestrator retry loop (e.g., `sim_harness/runner.py` / `sim_harness/orchestrator.py`)
- Trace metadata writer (`sim_harness/trace.py`)

## Acceptance checks
- Retry limit is configurable via CLI flag or `run_config`.
- Default behavior is **1 retry max per conversation test** (i.e., at most 2 total attempts including the initial attempt).
- Only retry on explicitly-defined retryable failures (e.g., timeout/5xx/transient network/OpenAI errors).
- Retry count and last failure reason are recorded in trace metadata.

## Constraints
- Do not retry schema/validation failures by default (unless explicitly decided), to avoid masking prompt regressions.
- Keep the default conservative (1) to control cost; callers can override.

## Links
- Parent epic: `be-sim`
- Related: `be-sim.5` (orchestrator), `be-sim.6` (trace store), `be-sim.9` (CI integration)

title: sim-harness: Expand golden scenarios to 20–30
description:
## Goal
Expand the golden scenario set from 3 to ~20–30 once the harness core loop is working.

## Context
After `be-sim.2` proves the framework with 3 scenarios, we want broader coverage to prevent overfitting and catch regressions.

## Acceptance checks
- Add 20–30 golden scenarios covering common failure modes (overwhelm, procrastination, low context, switching subjects, ack continuation, overview requests, etc.).
- All scenarios validate against the scenario schema.
- Scenarios are tagged (sv/en, subject, difficulty) so runs can filter subsets.

## Constraints
- Keep scenarios realistic and bounded in size.
- No fuzz set yet (optional later).

## Links
- Blocks: `be-sim.3`, `be-sim.4`, `be-sim.5`, `be-sim.7` (more coverage improves eval signal)
- Depends on: `be-sim.2`

title: sim-harness: Extended suite prompt + eval hardening
description:
## Problem
The extended suite currently fails when run against the real OpenAI coach due to (a) prompt/template bugs (language drift, missing mark_done, ack threading), and (b) evaluation semantics that check the last turn rather than the intended recommendation turn.

## Goal
Make the extended suite meaningful and stable for real-coach runs by tightening prompts and adjusting evaluation semantics (without weakening scenario intent).

## Definition of done
-  passes the extended suite reliably enough for iterative work (expect some flakiness, but core behaviors should hold).
- Prompt rules are explicit and internally consistent (language, ack continuation, mark-done, question discipline).
- Harness evaluation semantics align with scenario intent (per-turn where needed).

title: Fix coach prompt example: reply_language must not be hard-coded
description:
## Problem
In traces, the coach replies in Swedish to English user messages. The prompt template includes an example JSON with reply_language set to sv, which biases outputs.

## Deliverables
- Update coach prompt template to avoid hard-coded reply_language in examples (use null or placeholder).
- Add explicit rule: assistant_text must be written in reply_language; reply_language must match the student's latest message language.

## Acceptance criteria
- In sim traces, English user messages produce English assistant_text and reply_language=en.
- Scenario ext-006/ext-009/ext-010 no longer show Swedish replies for English input.

title: Reset conversation: optionally clear language_preference / preferred_subject / last_intent
description:
## Problem
Current reset clears chat_history + conversation_summary + last-selected ids, but leaves language_preference/preferred_subject/last_intent, which can continue biasing replies after a reset.

## Deliverables
- Extend reset behavior to support a true clean slate: clear language_preference, preferred_subject, last_intent (either always or behind a flag like clear_preferences=true).
- Add tests covering reset behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- After reset (with clear_preferences), user_state_json contains none of the cleared fields.
- Repeated test runs start from a consistent baseline.

title: User state: only persist language_preference when it matches server lang_hint
description:
## Problem
If the model outputs the wrong reply_language once, we persist it to user_state and that preference can become sticky and reinforce itself across turns.

## Deliverables
- Gate persistence of language_preference: only update when decision.reply_language matches server-side lang_hint (or other strong signal).
- If mismatch, do not update the stored preference (or set it to NULL).

## Acceptance criteria
- A single bad model reply_language does not permanently flip future replies.
- Debug exports show language_preference stays stable when reply_language mismatches lang_hint.

title: User state: recency/TTL guards for summary + last_selected thread continuation
description:
## Problem
Old user_state can cause the coach to over-index on stale selections/summaries (e.g., ack messages snapping back to an old assignment).

## Deliverables
- Use user_state.updated_at (or a dedicated timestamp) to apply TTLs:
  - If stale, omit conversation_summary from the prompt.
  - If stale, do not narrow candidates based on last_selected_assignment_id for acknowledgements.

## Acceptance criteria
- After a long idle period, the coach behaves like a fresh session unless the user re-establishes context.

title: User state API: allow explicit clearing of individual fields (avoid COALESCE stickiness)
description:
## Problem
upsert_user_state uses COALESCE so passing None cannot clear stored values. This makes it hard to intentionally reset/forget specific preferences.

## Deliverables
- Add explicit clear operations (e.g., clear_fields list, empty-string semantics, or dedicated setters) for language_preference / preferred_subject / last_intent / conversation_summary.

## Acceptance criteria
- Callers can reliably clear specific fields without wiping everything.

title: Conversation memory: consider structured summary (bounded recent_user_messages / extracted prefs)
description:
## Problem
Free-form summaries are hard to control and can accumulate bias. A structured, bounded representation improves determinism and reduces hallucination carry-over.

## Deliverables
- Propose and implement a minimal structured memory schema (e.g., recent_user_messages[], extracted preferences).
- Add migration/back-compat strategy (keep old conversation_summary optional during rollout).

## Acceptance criteria
- Prompt context becomes more predictable and easier to test.

title: Prompt: mark_done should auto-fire on single clear match (avoid unnecessary confirmation)
description:
## Problem
Even with mark_done rules, the coach sometimes asks for confirmation when there is a single obvious candidate match (e.g., user: 'I finished the English essay' and only one English essay candidate exists). This causes ext-010 to fail in sim-extended-openai.

## Deliverables
- Add explicit prompt rule: if exactly one candidate plausibly matches the completed item (courseName + title overlap), set mark_done_assignment_id immediately (no clarification).
- Only ask a clarifying question when multiple candidates match.

## Acceptance criteria
- ext-010 marks a-eng done without asking for confirmation.

title: sim-harness: SUT mode that calls real backend /chat/send (true persistence integration)
description:
## Problem
Current harness persistence simulation (injecting last_selected into user_state_json) improves prompt realism but does not exercise the real production persistence path (SQLite writes/reads + /chat/send ack logic + status overrides + summary updates).

## Goal
Add an integration SUT mode that runs scenarios by calling the real backend endpoint per turn so DB persistence and server rails are exercised end-to-end.

## Deliverables
- New SUT implementation (or mode flag) to call POST /chat/send each turn
  - Provide Authorization header using a deterministic session token (test-only)
  - Provide current_plan + user_message per turn
  - Capture response assistant_message + best_next_action
- Configurable backend base URL for local + Render
- Per-run isolated SQLite DB (e.g., set SQLITE_PATH per run)
- Ability to reset state between scenarios using POST /chat/reset (and optional clear_assignment_status)
- Trace artifacts record request/response and persisted IDs (selected/mark_done)

## Acceptance criteria
- A small integration suite (2–3 scenarios: ack continuation, mark-done, no-candidates fallback) runs through /chat/send and passes deterministically against a local backend.
- Optional: can run against Render (non-blocking; best-effort).

title: sim-backend: optional mode to use real OpenAI coach (persistence + OpenAI end-to-end)
description:
## Problem
sim-backend currently patches the coach to a deterministic stub so it can exercise /chat/send + SQLite persistence offline. This is great for determinism, but it does not validate the full end-to-end path of persistence + real OpenAI behavior together.

## Goal
Add a flag/mode to the backend integration runner to run against the real OpenAI coach while still using the real backend endpoints (/chat/reset + /chat/send) and SQLite persistence.

## Deliverables
- Add CLI flag to sim_harness.cli backend (and a Makefile target) such as:
  - --use-openai-coach (default false)
  - --backend-base-url or --in-process/--http selection
- When --use-openai-coach is enabled:
  - Do NOT patch coach_decide / coach_decide_with_raw
  - Do NOT override OPENAI_API_KEY
  - Respect existing backend env (including DEBUG_EXPORT_ENABLED behavior)
- Still reset state between scenarios via /chat/reset (optionally with clear flags).
- Trace output includes request/response, selected ids, mark_done ids, and run config.

## Acceptance criteria
- New mode can run the integration suite end-to-end against local backend with real OpenAI (best-effort; may be flaky).
- Documented usage and example commands.

title: Coach prompt: enforce exactly one '?' in assistant_text (ext-006)
description:
## Problem
In sim-extended-openai, ext-006 fails because the coach uses multiple question marks when asking a clarifying question.

## Proposed fix
Tighten coach prompt one-question discipline:
- When asking a clarifying question, write exactly ONE sentence that ends with '?' (one '?' total).
- Any supporting text must be statements (no additional '?').
- Provide an example for the 'easy' clarifier phrasing that uses one '?' total.

## Acceptance
- ext-006 passes in sim-extended-openai (max_question_marks=1).

title: Coach prompt: completion should mark done on single clear match (ext-010)
description:
## Problem
In sim-extended-openai, ext-010 sometimes asks for confirmation instead of setting mark_done_assignment_id, even when there is a single clear match (English essay vs English essay draft).

## Proposed fix
Strengthen coach prompt completion matching:
- If the student says they finished something and there is exactly one plausible matching candidate by courseName and/or title keyword overlap, set mark_done_assignment_id immediately.
- Do not ask a confirmation question in the single-match case.
- Add an explicit example: 'I finished the English essay' + candidate 'English essay draft' => mark_done_assignment_id=a-eng.

## Acceptance
- ext-010 passes in sim-extended-openai reliably.

title: Prompt: Acknowledgement must continue the previously selected assignment
description:
## Problem
On acknowledgement turns (ok/ja/yes), the model often sets selected_assignment_id=null and re-asks the user, breaking threading and failing selection expectations.

## Deliverables
- Strengthen the coach system prompt: if previous turn recommended/selected an assignment and student replies with acknowledgement, selected_assignment_id must repeat the same id and assistant continues with the next tiny step.

## Acceptance criteria
- For ext-004/ext-009, when the student replies Ok/Okej after a recommendation, the decision keeps selected_assignment_id and continues the same task.

title: sim-harness: run suites across multiple OpenAI models (model matrix)
description:
## Problem
We want to evaluate coach behavior across different OpenAI models (quality/cost/latency tradeoffs) using the same scenario suites, and compare results.

## Deliverables
- Allow specifying the OpenAI model for harness runs (env var override or CLI flag):
  - sim_harness.cli quick/extended/backend --openai-model MODEL_NAME
  - or OPENAI_MODEL=MODEL_NAME
- Ensure trace summary includes the model name used.
- Add convenience Makefile targets/examples for running a model matrix:
  - e.g., make sim-extended-openai MODEL=gpt-4.1-mini and MODEL=gpt-4.1.
- Optional: lightweight report that groups pass/fail counts by model.

## Acceptance criteria
- You can run the same suite against 2+ models without editing code.
- Traces and summaries record which model was used.

title: Prompt: Mark done when student says they finished something (candidate matching)
description:
## Problem
When the student explicitly says they finished an assignment, the model congratulates but often leaves mark_done_assignment_id null.

## Deliverables
- Add explicit rule + example: if student says finished/completed/submitted, set mark_done_assignment_id to the best-matching candidate id (courseName + title overlap).
- Ask at most one clarifying question only if no candidate matches.

## Acceptance criteria
- ext-010 sets mark_done_assignment_id=a-eng.

title: Prompt: One-question discipline (max one '?')
description:
## Problem
The coach frequently asks multiple questions in one message (or uses multiple question marks), violating the one-question rule and scenario constraints (ext-006).

## Deliverables
- Add explicit formatting guidance: ask at most one question and use at most one '?' character in assistant_text.
- Provide an example phrasing for offering two options in a single question.

## Acceptance criteria
- ext-006 assistant_text contains at most one '?' per turn.

title: Policy alignment: interpret 'easy' (clarify-first vs shortest-task) and update prompt/scenario
description:
## Problem
Scenario ext-006 currently expects no selection + one clarifying question for 'I want something easy', but the model reasonably selects the shortest estimatedMinutes task. We need a product decision and alignment.

Deliverables
- Decide desired behavior for 'easy':
  - Clarify-first: ask one clarifying question, selected_assignment_id=null
  - Or shortest-task: select the shortest estimatedMinutes candidate
- Update coach prompt (and scenario ext-006 expectations if needed) to match the decision.

Acceptance criteria
- ext-006 passes consistently under the chosen policy.

title: Harness eval semantics: support turn-level expectations (avoid last-turn false negatives)
description:
## Problem
Some scenarios select the correct assignment on turn 0 but later output selected_assignment_id=null, causing scenario-level expectations (checked at end-of-run) to fail (ext-004/ext-009).

## Deliverables
- Add support for turn-level expectations in ScenarioExpected (e.g., expected_selected_assignment_id_by_turn).
- Alternatively add scenario knob for which turn to validate selection on (e.g., validate_turn=0).

## Acceptance criteria
- ext-004/ext-009 validate the intended recommendation turn and stop failing due to later null selections.

title: Harness: persist last_selected_assignment_id into user_state between turns
description:
## Problem
In the harness, user_state stays empty between turns, so the model has less signal to keep selections sticky on acknowledgement turns.

## Deliverables
- After each coach decision with selected_assignment_id set, inject last_selected_assignment_id into subsequent turns' user_state payload.

## Acceptance criteria
- Multi-turn scenarios show user_state reflecting the last selection in the next turn's prompt.

title: Backend safety rails: recover from null selection on ack and missing mark_done
description:
## Problem
Even with prompt improvements, occasional model slips are likely. We can harden UX by applying small post-processing rails.

## Deliverables
- If student message is an acknowledgement and server has last_selected_assignment_id, override a null selected_assignment_id to that value.
- If student message indicates completion and mark_done_assignment_id is null, attempt best-match heuristic or a single retry.

## Acceptance criteria
- Acknowledgement turns no longer lose the thread even if the model outputs null.
- Explicit completion messages reliably mark the intended assignment done.

title: User state: sanitize legacy conversation_summary on read (strip assistant lines)
description:
## Problem
Legacy conversation_summary rows may contain assistant text (A: ...) and other stale content. Even though new writes are user-only, old summaries can still be injected into prompts and cause sticky hallucinations / thread lock-in.

## Deliverables
- Sanitize conversation_summary before sending it to the coach prompt: keep only user lines (e.g., lines starting with 'U:').
- Add a regression test using a stored legacy summary that contains assistant lines and ensure the prompt receives only user lines.

## Acceptance criteria
- Debug exports show conversation_summary contains only user lines.
- Previously 'sticky' assistant content no longer appears in coach prompts.

title: sim-harness.2 — Scenario schema + “golden set” dataset v1 (P0)
description:
## Goal
Define a minimal scenario format + a tiny “golden set” so we can prove the harness works end-to-end before scaling up.

## Context
In `be-sim`, a **scenario** is a structured test case that seeds a simulated student↔coach conversation. It provides:
- student persona/context (language, motivation)
- assignment list (candidates/source of truth)
- constraints (time/energy)
- evaluation hints (what counts as a good coach response)

This is the foundation for:
- the student simulator (`be-sim.4`)
- the orchestrator (`be-sim.5`)
- evaluators (`be-sim.7`)

## Acceptance checks
- A scenario schema exists and fixtures validate against it.
- Scenario loader can load scenarios by `scenario_id` deterministically.
- A “golden set” of **3 scenarios** exists (to keep scope small for first rollout).
- Each of the 3 scenarios has clear expected outcomes (rubric hints / hard checks).

## Constraints
- Keep fixtures small and human-editable (JSON or YAML).
- Do not require CI for initial rollout; must run locally.

## Links
- Parent epic: `be-sim`
- Follow-up expansion ticket should add 20–30 scenarios once the harness loop is proven.

title: sim-harness.3 — Study Buddy SUT wrapper (prompt + deterministic rails) (P0)
description:
## Problem
You need a consistent “System Under Test” API so the harness can swap prompt versions and track outputs.

## Deliverables
- `StudyBuddyClient` wrapper that accepts:
  - prompt version id
  - scenario context
  - conversation history
- Deterministic rails:
  - strict output validation (JSON schema or required fields)
  - fallback behavior logged (e.g., “asked clarifying question”, “returned safe default plan”)
- Capture model parameters (temperature/top_p/seed if applicable)

## Acceptance criteria
- Can run two prompt versions against the same scenario and produce comparable trace output.
- Every response is either “valid” or “invalid with reason + fallback path recorded”.

## Depends on
- sim-harness.1
- sim-harness.2

title: sim-harness.4 — Student simulator v1 (hybrid state machine + LLM text) (P0)
description:
## Problem
Pure LLM student sims are noisy; pure scripted sims are unrealistic. Hybrid gives control + realism.

## Deliverables
- Student hidden state:
  - motivation ∈ [0..1], confusion ∈ [0..1], time_remaining, resistance_mode, etc.
- State machine controlling intent:
  - stall, ask for answer, agree then disappear, overwhelm, minimal replies
- LLM rendering layer producing natural language without revealing hidden state
- Determinism knobs:
  - fixed random seeds
  - low temperature for golden set gating runs

## Acceptance criteria
- Given same scenario + seed, the student agent produces repeatable messages (within defined tolerance).
- Simulator can enforce behaviors like “resist for first 2 turns”.

## Depends on
- sim-harness.2

title: sim-harness.5 — Conversation orchestrator + stop conditions (P0)
description:
## Problem
You need a reliable runner that alternates agents, enforces max turns, and determines terminal state.

## Deliverables
- Orchestrator that runs:
  - student → study buddy → student … for N turns
- Stop conditions:
  - plan created (detected by rubric tags/structure)
  - student quits
  - max turns reached
- Batch runner:
  - run one scenario
  - run suite (all golden)
  - run A/B comparison across two prompt versions

## Acceptance criteria
- `make quick` runs a small subset (e.g., 5 scenarios).
- Orchestrator emits per-run outcome: `success|partial|fail` + reason.

## Depends on
- sim-harness.3
- sim-harness.4

title: sim-harness.6 — Trace store + artifact format (P0)
description:
## Problem
Prompt optimization is impossible if traces are missing crucial inputs (tools, retrieved data, validation failures).

## Deliverables
- Trace schema (JSONL recommended):
  - run_id, scenario_id, prompt_version
  - per-turn: messages, tool calls, tool outputs, validation results
  - cost/latency/token counts (if available)
- Local storage layout:
  - `runs/YYYY-MM-DD/<run_id>/trace.jsonl`
  - `runs/.../summary.json` (aggregated metrics)

## Acceptance criteria
- Every run produces trace artifacts automatically.
- Runs can be reproduced from stored metadata (prompt version + scenario + seed).

## Depends on
- sim-harness.5

title: sim-harness.7 — Evaluators v1: hard checks + rubric judge (P0)
description:
## Problem
You need fast, reliable gating metrics, plus a more nuanced evaluator for quality.

## Deliverables
### 1) Hard checks (deterministic)
- schema validity
- “one best next action” present
- includes time-bounded starter task (10–20 min) OR explicitly explains why not
- tone constraints (no shame, no policy violations)

### 2) LLM judge (rubric)
- actionability, clarity, reduces cognitive load, autonomy support
- pairwise mode for A/B comparisons

### 3) Aggregator
Outputs:
- per-scenario score
- overall pass rate
- regression flags compared to baseline prompt

## Acceptance criteria
- “Quick suite” fails CI if hard checks regress beyond threshold.
- Judge outputs stored with trace for audit.

## Depends on
- sim-harness.6

title: sim-harness.8 — Reporting: dashboards + diff views (P1)
description:
## Problem
If results aren’t readable, you won’t iterate fast.

## Deliverables
- HTML/Markdown report generator:
  - summary metrics
  - top regressions
  - interesting failures (invalid schema, student drop-off, etc.)
  - per-scenario A/B transcript diff
- Optional: small UI/notebook for browsing runs

## Acceptance criteria
- After `make ab`, you get a single report file you can open and scan quickly.

## Depends on
- sim-harness.7

title: sim-harness.9 — CI integration (nightly full suite + PR quick suite) (P1)
description:
## Problem
Without CI gates, you’ll ship regressions when prompts change.

## Deliverables
- CI job: quick suite on every PR
- CI job: full suite nightly (golden + fuzz)
- Artifact upload (traces + report)

## Acceptance criteria
- PRs show pass/fail with a link to the report artifact.

## Depends on
- sim-harness.7
- sim-harness.8

title: Chat conversation improvements
description: Improve chat coherence so the coach reliably answers the latest user message and doesn’t over-index on stale/hallucinated prior context. Focus areas: rolling summary safety, prompt guardrails, and regression tests.

title: Fix rolling conversation_summary to avoid persisting assistant hallucinations
description:
## Root cause
The rolling summary is currently built by appending BOTH user and assistant text each turn. If the assistant ever hallucinates or states something incorrectly, that content becomes sticky context and can distort future replies.

Code reference: backend/app/routes/chat.py:_update_rolling_summary

## Proposed fixes to evaluate (choose one)
- Store only user messages / user-confirmed facts in summary
- Or remove rolling summary entirely and rely on explicit state (last_selected_assignment_id, done map, preferred subject)
- Or replace with structured state fields + a safer summarizer (server-side, fact-only)

## Acceptance
- Summary no longer amplifies assistant mistakes across turns
- Add regression test: earlier assistant hallucination must NOT be repeated as fact later

title: Prompt guardrails: prioritize latest message; restrict facts from history/summary
description:
## Problem
Even with warnings, the model may still treat conversation_history / conversation_summary as factual and “continue the prior story” instead of answering the latest user message.

## Proposed changes
- Strengthen coach prompt: explicitly prioritize the latest Student message over any earlier context.
- Add hard rule: never assert completion/progress unless (a) the user said it in the latest message, or (b) it’s reflected in current candidate/status signals.
- Consider excluding conversation_summary entirely from the prompt (or moving it to a lower-priority section).

## Acceptance
- Regression test: when the latest user message changes subject/intention, assistant response follows it.
- Reduced instances of “you already finished X” unless supported by current signals.

title: History/summary shaping: reduce or reweight stale assistant context
description:
## Problem
Our history signals can amplify mistakes:
- conversation_history includes assistant messages (which can contain hallucinations)
- conversation_summary persists assistant text across turns

## Proposed changes
- Consider passing only user turns in conversation_history, or tagging assistant turns as "untrusted".
- Consider shrinking the history window further for short interactions.
- Add an explicit “last_user_message_only” field or separator in the prompt.

## Acceptance
- Model continues threads correctly on ack, but otherwise responds to the latest message.
- Regression tests cover both ack and non-ack flows.

title: Add 'Reset conversation' capability (backend + iOS)
description:
## Problem
There is no easy way for users (or the app) to reset the conversation if the coach gets stuck in a stale thread.

## Proposed changes
- Add an API endpoint to clear chat_history + conversation_summary for a user (or a "reset" flag on /chat/send).
- Add iOS UI affordance (Settings or Chat screen) to reset conversation.

## Acceptance
- Reset clears persisted conversation_summary and history for that user.
- After reset, coach responses do not reference prior conversation.

title: Regression tests: prevent stale-context answers
description:
## Goal
Add automated tests that reproduce the reported failure mode: the coach answers using stale prior context instead of the latest message.

## Scenarios
- Previous assistant message contains a wrong claim; later turns must not repeat it as fact.
- Latest user message changes subject (e.g., 'English') and assistant must follow it.
- Ack flow ('ok/ja') should continue the same thread.

## Acceptance
- New tests fail on current behavior and pass after fixes.
